## A stale release PR

Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run the failed `Release` workflow, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is retried up to four times before it fails.

If a stale release PR was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the merge consumed no changesets, and every later push to `main` retries it. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.

# Specifications

Each spec (`spec@1`) states current behavior as testable criteria, grouped by topic prefix. No history: Git records how the behavior got here, and [`docs/adr/`](../adr/README.md) records the design decisions that still hold.

| Spec | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [`workspace.json`](workspace.json) | Root and member discovery, package identity, per-package config rules, npm platform packages |
| [`versioning.json`](versioning.json) | Changeset format, severity aggregation, cascade, groups, prerelease, snapshot, applying versions, changelogs, the release decision file |
| [`release.json`](release.json) | `callisto release`, the CI route, decision authority, operation order, registry publish and observation, reruns, tags and GitHub releases, the managed release PR |
| [`cli.json`](cli.json) | Command surface, output and exit codes, `status`, `add`, `init`, generated workflows, `pre`, `snapshot`, `completions`, `schema` |
| [`matrix.json`](matrix.json) | `callisto matrix`: native build targets and runtime constraints for CI |

`REQ-DX-V1.md` is the open v1 requirement; delete it when v1 ships.

How the code implements these specs: [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) and [`docs/architecture/`](../architecture/).

When code and a spec disagree, reproduce the behavior first. Fix the spec if the intended contract changed; otherwise fix the code.

Remaining v1 work is in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md). Behavior not yet implemented, such as co-located Cargo/Maturin version derivation, lives in [the scoped design](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md). content.text:
The retry, the stale-PR hold, the tests, the spec entries and the docs are all in draft PR #425 on trail #162. The first real test is the first push to `main` after it merges.

**What changed:**
- **Retries (step 2):** the release PR refresh now retries transient GitHub errors four times, waiting 2, 4 and 8 seconds, and prints each failed attempt's stderr.
- **A bug the tests turned up:** when `gh pr list` failed, the script kept going and died later in `jq` with an unrelated error. It now stops with `gh`'s own error.
- **Safe commit retries:** before each retry of the commit mutation, the staging branch goes back to the base commit, so a success that GitHub never acknowledged can't fail the retry. `gh pr create` and the staging cleanup are the only calls that don't retry.
- **The guard (step 3):** a new `Hold release PR` workflow turns the open release PR into a draft on every push to `main`. The refresh marks it ready only if it was built from the current tip. A failed or skipped refresh leaves a draft, and GitHub won't merge a draft.
- **Why a draft and not a status check:** a ruleset can't scope a required check to one head branch, so a status check would have blocked every other PR. The draft needs no repo setting.

entire checkpoint push — Upload waiting checkpoints now
Upload the named checkpoints to the checkpoint sync remote now, the same way
git push would. Use it when the clone's checkpoint push policy is manual, so
git push leaves checkpoints on this machine, or to upload ahead of your next
push under automatic.

Each checkpoint is uploaded at its current version, with every earlier version
not yet uploaded. Run 'entire checkpoint list --outgoing' to see what is
waiting. <checkpoint-id>@<commit> uploads that checkpoint only while <commit>
is still its current version: if it changed since you looked, it is not sent.

--all and a bare <checkpoint-id> need a terminal. Without one, name each
checkpoint as <checkpoint-id>@<commit>, using the commit --outgoing --json
reports. With no arguments, it lists what is waiting and uploads nothing.

Examples:
  entire checkpoint push <id>
  entire checkpoint push --all
  entire checkpoint push <id>@<commit> --json

When to use this:
Uploads checkpoints the user may be keeping on this machine on purpose.
Never run this unless the user explicitly asks to upload those checkpoints.
Without a terminal it accepts only <checkpoint-id>@<commit>; get the commit
from `checkpoints[].commit` in `entire checkpoint list --outgoing --json`.
A result with status `changed` means the checkpoint moved since that read:
read the listing again and ask the user before uploading the new version.

content.content:
MERGED: fix(release): do not tag a published version onto a later commit
The A2 defect from the v1 review, reproduced on merged main with a stand-in `cargo` and `git`: a release stopped after publishing (the tag push failed), an unrelated commit landed, and the rerun on that newer commit printed "already published; skipping" and tagged the newer commit. The tag then pointed at code the registry never received.

A local `callisto release` now finds the commit that set each package's release version (the newest commit whose manifest holds the version while its parent's does not) and checks whether the package has commits after it. Only if it does, and the registry already holds the version, it refuses with E320 before any effect, naming the version commit and the fix: check that commit out and run `callisto release` again. Verified the same way: from the version commit the rerun adopts the published version (no second publish) and tags that commit.

It never refuses without evidence: a package untouched since its version commit, a version the registry does not hold, an inherited or unreadable version, or a preview with no `origin` to observe all proceed as before. Nothing is observed unless a package moved, so ordinary releases make no extra registry calls.

Not changed: the managed route, which already releases the exact merge commit, and a package the previous run tagged on HEAD, which still resumes.

Tests: three unit tests for finding the version commit (untouched, later commit, commit in another package) and an end-to-end test over the fake pub
PR MERGED: fix(release): do not tag a published version onto a later commit

# OIDC trusted publishing

Plan, not behavior: nothing here ships before it is built, and the specs describe only what exists. Target: after v1. Delete this file when the work ships.

## Goal

Publish to npm, crates.io and PyPI with no long-lived registry secret in the repository. The CI job proves its identity with a short-lived GitHub OIDC token, and each registry accepts it for a package that names that repository and workflow as a trusted publisher.

## What each registry needs

| Registry | Trusted publisher is set up | The job must | Token reaches the tool by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm | per package on npmjs.com: owner, repository, workflow file, optional environment | have `id-token: write`; run npm 11.5.1 or later (Node 24 ships it) | npm detects the OIDC environment itself and prefers it over a token. No secret |
| crates.io | per crate in its settings, after a first manual publish | have `id-token: write`; run `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`, which exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived crates.io token and revokes it when the job ends | the action's `token` output, passed to `cargo publish` as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` |
| PyPI | per project on pypi.org: owner, repository, workflow file, optional environment | have `id-token: write`; mint an upload token through PyPI's OIDC exchange | PyPI documents the exchange as an implementation detail; the stable interfaces are `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` and `uv publish`. Twine takes the minted token as `TWINE_PASSWORD` with `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` |

A mismatch in owner, repository, workflow file or environment fails, and npm reports it as a misleading E404. Self-hosted runners are not supported by npm. crates.io blocks the `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` triggers.

## Where Callisto stands

- Generated workflows already give `execute` `id-token: write` (for npm provenance), so the permission itself is not new there. Callisto's own release workflow does not: its policy check allows `id-token: write` only on `build-artifact`.
- Callisto passes the environment through to the tool and never strips `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` or `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`, so npm can see them. ADR 4 keeps authentication with the ecosystem tool, which fits: Callisto does not need to mint tokens.
- The generated action writes a temporary npm config with an `NPM_TOKEN` entry. With no token set that line may stop npm falling back to OIDC. Unverified.
- Twine is the PyPI uploader, and it cannot mint a token.

## Work

1. Decide the shape: a `callisto.toml` switch, or a generated-workflow option, for "this registry publishes by OIDC", so no secret input is expected for it.
2. npm: omit the token entry from the generated npm config when OIDC is chosen, and check the pnpm, yarn and bun publish paths. Only `npm publish` is documented to use OIDC, so each package manager must be tested.
3. crates.io: generate the auth-action step before `execute` and pass its output as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.
4. PyPI: mint the token in a generated step, or use `uv publish` where it is available; keep twine for the token path.
5. Diagnostics: an E163 hint for the npm E404 case that names the trusted-publisher fields to recheck.
6. Policy and docs: the release workflow policy check, `docs/publishing.md`, the init docs and the generated-workflow tests.

## Decisions for the owner

- Callisto's own workflow: allow `id-token: write` on `execute`? With OIDC there is no registry secret at all, which is the intent of "only `execute` gets registry secrets", but the policy check forbids the permission and changing it is the owner's call. A GitHub Environment stays out either way.
- One job holds the OIDC permission while the project's own build code runs (cargo build scripts during `cargo publish` verification, npm lifecycle scripts). That is also true of a long-lived token today, and a short-lived scoped token is strictly less exposed. Keeping the build in a separate job (the current build-artifact split) limits it further.

## Verification

Needs real packages, so it is owner-run. For each registry: configure a scratch package's trusted publisher, run a release from a scratch repository with no token set, and confirm the version appears and the tag and release are created. Include a deliberately wrong workflow name per registry and check the diagnostic. Local registries (Verdaccio, pypiserver, cargo-http-registry) cannot exercise OIDC, so they cover only the no-token configuration paths.

## Sources

- npm: https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers
- crates.io: https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action and https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/07/11/crates-io-development-update-2025-07
- PyPI: https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/using-a-publisher/

40	pub fn last_failed_command() -> Option<String> {
41	    LAST_FAILED_COMMAND.lock().ok().and_then(|last| last.clone())
42	}
43	
44	/// Caps how much of a subprocess's stdout/stderr this process will retain
45	/// in memory. The pipe is still drained in full past this point (bytes
46	/// beyond the cap are read and discarded, never accumulated) so a chatty
47	/// child can never deadlock waiting on a full OS pipe buffer -- this
48	/// bounds memory, not duration (`PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_SECS` bounds that
49	/// separately).
50	const MAX_CAPTURED_OUTPUT_BYTES: usize = 10 * 1024 * 1024;
51	
52	const RELEASE_CREDENTIALS: &[&str] = &[
53	    // The job's OIDC request: only npm needs it, to attach provenance.
54	    "ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN",
55	    "ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL",
56	    "CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN",
57	    "GH_TOKEN",
58	    "GITHUB_TOKEN",
59	    "NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN",
60	    "NPM_TOKEN",
61	    "NODE_AUTH_TOKEN",
62	    "PYPI_TOKEN",
63	    "CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG",
64	    "TWINE_USERNAME",
65	    "TWINE_PASSWORD",
66	];
67	
68	const ACTION_SECRET_INPUTS: &[&str] = &[
69	    "CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN",
70	    "GH_TOKEN",
71	    "GITHUB_TOKEN",
72	    "NPM_TOKEN",
73	    "PYPI_TOKEN",
74	    "CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG",
75	    "TWINE_USERNAME",
76	    "TWINE_PASSWORD",
77	];
78	
79	struct ChildEnvironment<'a> {
80	    remove: &'a [&'a str],
81	    set: &'a [(&'a str, &'a str)],
82	}
83	
84	/// The release credentials a tool reads from its own environment. Every other release
85	/// credential is removed from its child process, so a tool never sees a secret it does not use.
86	/// A tool absent here needs none; publishers receive theirs explicitly instead.
87	fn credentials_needed_by(tool: &str) -> &'static [&'static str] {
88	    match tool {
89	        "npm" | "pnpm" | "yarn" | "bun" => &[
90	            "NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN",
91	            "NPM_TOKEN",
92	            "NODE_AUTH_TOKEN",
93	            "ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN",
94	            "ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL",
95	        ],
96	        "cargo" => &["CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN"],
97	        // `gh` reads GH_TOKEN, and GITHUB_TOKEN when that is unset; it runs the attestation
98	        // check and every forge call, and refuses to run without a token.
99	        "gh" => &["GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN"],
100	        _ => &[],
101	    }
102	}
103	
104	fn unrelated_credentials(program: &str) -> Vec<&'static str> {
105	    let tool = tool_name(program);
106	    let keep = credentials_needed_by(tool);
107	    RELEASE_CREDENTIALS

# Next work

Local only, never PR it. Rewritten 2026-11-02 after the 0.17.0 release and the E165 wedge; earlier plans are in `archive/`. In-repo roadmap: `docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`.

## State

- 0.17.0 is released (GitHub release, crates.io). `macos-latest` is used for every macOS runner; ubuntu is `ubuntu-latest` except `ubuntu-24.04-arm`.
- 2026-11-02 incident (trail 162): #409 was built from changesets that #420 rewrote, and its refresh failed on one GitHub 5xx. The stale PR merged, consumed nothing, and every Release run failed with E165 until #423 reverted the release payload. Fixed in #425: forge retries in `create-or-update-release-pr.sh`, a `Hold release PR` workflow that drafts the open release PR on every push to main, and the refresh marks it ready only when built from the current tip. First real run of the hold workflow was queued after #425 merged: verify it ran (and that `gh pr ready` and `--undo` behave) before trusting it.
- Performance: no regression at scale. A/B of #365 against main at 10,000 packages is inside noise (6 to 10 s run to run, git time dominates, process counts equal). At 400 packages `status` is about 20 ms (13%) slower on main, repeatable; suspects are #418 and #415, not bisected. Do not optimize without a measured A/B.
- Closed by checking source: #290 guard gaps (version_commit.rs compares tree content, the git log has no 100 cap). The `<crate>@0` stray tags are deleted. The 10-20 spec drift list was partly addressed by #410 and #417; not re-verified in full.

## Open, not blocked

- Verify the first runs of the hold workflow and the next release PR refresh (see State).
- Private workspace root `package.json` is listed as a package (`npm/monorepo`). Needs the owner's choice of exclusion shape (lean: `[[package]] match = "npm/monorepo"` with `ignore = true`).
- Fixed group cannot share one tag or one GitHub release title (E194). Design pass: ADR 9 and 12.
- Spec drift: re-run `scribe:spec-drift` per spec; release.json first.
- T12: production-path registry tests for Cargo and PyPI bypass binding; `registry_endpoint.rs` rejects non-https, loopback included. Decide the approach or drop it.
- Release target table: `matrix.rs` has its own 18 triples instead of rustc target facts (small).
- E165 hint: the error text could point at the revert recovery in `docs/releasing.md`. `docs/errors.md` is generated from `error.rs`, so change both.
- 400-package `status` 20 ms gap: bisect only if wanted.

## Waiting on michi

- `ready_by_edge` is on michi main but not in a release (0.6.0 is the latest). When released: replace the `eligible_in` ancestor check and `is_registry_effect` with `Needs::Issued` and `Needs::Confirmed` edge kinds. No path dependency in a PR.
- michi-pipeline is not adopted: its steps need `'static` ownership and Callisto's providers are borrowed.

## Owner decisions open

- OIDC trusted publishing (`docs/projects/OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md`), npm first. Needs: the config shape (`callisto.toml` switch or generated-workflow option) and whether Callisto's own release workflow may hold `id-token: write` on `execute`. Checked 2026-11-02: the npm worry in the plan is moot, because `run-release.sh` writes the `_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}` line only when `NPM_TOKEN` is non-empty, and `runner.rs` already passes the OIDC request variables to npm, pnpm, yarn and bun only. Real verification needs the owner's packages.
- Accept ADR 12 (conditions met per the 2026-10-23 check); ADR 11's partial revision.
- Enable GitHub immutable releases; Entire `push_sessions` and `push_checkpoints`; the no-output publish limit.
- Private and HTML-only PyPI; npm channel promotion; checksums; wrapper bump severity; inferred-only releases (ADR 2); release-commit provenance.
- Decided: lockstep versioning, all four crates to 1.0, libraries documented internal; pre mode refused on the managed route (E318); W4 print-only redacted tail; macOS runners follow `macos-latest`.

## Housekeeping

- Local worktrees still to decide: `smoke-main` (441 tracked files deleted in the working tree), `wf_cd627354-1a0-2` (2 commits not in main, one untracked test file), `callisto-homebrew-tap` (untracked `notify-homebrew.yml`), `entire-hooks-update`; branch `stack/docs-v1` (8 commits not in main).
- Open Entire trails whose callisto changes are all merged: 129, 139, 141 to 148, 151, 152, 159, 160, 163 (closing was blocked by the auto-mode classifier; close them yourself or allow it). Trail 162 closes after the hold workflow is verified.
- The `uses: $/.github/actions/...` lines in the workflows: confirm what they are before touching them.

## Rules

- Read `AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the matching `docs/architecture/` topic and `docs/adr/README.md` first.
- One `just ci` at a time. No parallel cargo builds in one checkout.
- Measure before building an optimization (see memory: measure-value-before-building).
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link`). No force pushes, no session links, one line per Markdown paragraph.
- Worktree sessions: `/usr/bin/git`, plain commands, scripts written with the Write tool. Sandboxed shells cannot write to a second worktree, to `~/.claude/jobs`, or sign commits.
- A release PR is only mergeable when it is not a draft; merge it, then let the Release run finish before merging anything else.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
# commit API, on the staging branch.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# One GitHub 5xx must not strand the release PR until the next push to main: retry transient failures,
# print every failed attempt's stderr, and leave other failures (404, 422) to the caller. `gh pr create`
# is not wrapped, because a retry after an unseen success would fail on the PR it just made.
gh_retry() {
  local attempt=1 delay=2 err code
  err=$(mktemp)
  until gh "$@" 2> "$err"; do
    code=$?
    cat "$err" >&2
    if [[ $attempt -ge 4 ]] || ! grep -qiE 'Something went wrong|HTTP 5[0-9]{2}|Bad Gateway|Service Unavailable|Gateway Time|timed? ?out|connection reset|unexpected EOF' "$err"; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return "$code"
    fi
    echo "::warning::gh $1 hit a transient GitHub error (attempt $attempt of 4); retrying in ${delay}s" >&2
    sleep "$delay"
    delay=$((delay * 2))
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    [[ -z "${RETRY_RESET:-}" ]] || "$RETRY_RESET" || true
  done
  cat "$err" >&2
  rm -f "$err"
}

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs
  # Command substitutions do not inherit set -e, so a failed read must stop here, not later in jq.
  raw_prs=$(gh_retry pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid) || return $?
  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    '{
      schemaVersion: 2,
      repository: $repository,
      baseBranch: $base_branch,
      baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
        number,
        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
        headBranch: .headRefName,
        headCommit: .headRefOid
      }]
    }'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh_retry pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
else
  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
fi

read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
command+=(--emit-decision "$INPUT_DECISION_PATH")
"${command[@]}"
git add -A
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }

plan_file=$(mktemp)
callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
local_tree=$(git write-tree)

staging_created=false
cleanup_staging() {
  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
  fi
  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
}
trap cleanup_staging EXIT

# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

reset_staging() {
  gh_retry api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" -F force=true > /dev/null 2>&1
}

if reset_staging; then
  :
else
  gh_retry api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
fi
staging_created=true

jq -n \
  --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
  '{
    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
    variables: {
      input: {
        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
        message: {headline: $headline},
        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
        fileChanges: {
          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
        }
      }
    }
  }' > body.json

# A retry may follow a commit the forge made but never acknowledged, which would fail the mutation's
# expectedHeadOid, so each retry first puts the staging branch back on the base commit.
new_sha=$(RETRY_RESET=reset_staging gh_retry api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
remote_tree=$(gh_retry api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
  gh_retry api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
else
  if ! gh_retry api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    gh_retry api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
  fi
fi
moved_sha=$(gh_retry api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" --jq '.object.sha')
if [[ "$moved_sha" != "$new_sha" ]]; then
  echo "::error::$release_branch points at $moved_sha after the update, expected $new_sha; a concurrent write may have raced this run"
  exit 1
fi

if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
  # The PR list can lag a ref move by a moment, and a stale read looks like a changed snapshot.
  # A real concurrent change stays visible, so the last attempt still fails.
  verified=false
  for _ in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9; do
    if callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" \
      --applied-head "$new_sha" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      verified=true
      break
    fi
    sleep 3
  done
  if [[ "$verified" != true ]]; then
    callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" \
      --applied-head "$new_sha" > /dev/null
  fi
else
  callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
fi

label_exists=$(gh_retry label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
  gh_retry label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
fi

case "$decision_kind" in
  create)
    create_args=(--head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL")
    pr_url=$(gh pr create "${create_args[@]}")
    echo "$pr_url"
    pr_number=${pr_url##*/}
    ;;
  update)
    edit_args=(--title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL")
    gh_retry pr edit "$existing_pr" "${edit_args[@]}"
    pr_number=$existing_pr
    ;;
esac

# The hold workflow drafts the release PR whenever main moves, because a draft cannot be merged. Hand it back only
# when it was built from the current tip; if main moved again during this run, it stays a draft for the next run.
is_draft=$(gh_retry pr view "$pr_number" --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft')
tip=$(gh_retry api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/ref/heads/$INPUT_BRANCH" --jq '.object.sha')
if [[ "$tip" == "$base_commit" ]]; then
  if [[ "$is_draft" == true ]]; then gh_retry pr ready "$pr_number"; fi
else
  echo "::warning::$INPUT_BRANCH moved to $tip while this run built the release PR from $base_commit; leaving it a draft for the next run"
  if [[ "$is_draft" != true ]]; then gh_retry pr ready "$pr_number" --undo; fi
fi

content.text:
The spec-drift fixes are in PR #427 on trail #173, and nothing else is open. I haven't seen CI on it yet. The re-check found 20 of 253 criteria drifted (matrix 0 of 24, cli 3 of 55, workspace 2 of 39, versioning 4 of 62, release 11 of 73). That is about 8%, down from the 14% in the 2026-10-20 review.

**Fixed in #427:**
- **Code:**
  - `completions` no longer offers a `help` subcommand.
  - `init` prints its warnings in text mode.
  - A private root `package.json` that starts with a byte-order mark is no longer listed as a package.
  - E115 names the real `pre.json` path.
  - E165 now points at the stale-release-PR recovery.
- **Two bugs in my own #425, now fixed:**
  - A failed PR read before verification passed an empty snapshot on. It now stops with `gh`'s own status.
  - A new release PR was created ready before the tip check. It is now created as a draft.
- **Spec corrections where the code was right:**
  - The inherited-version write goes into the member.
  - A missing group member is E108.
  - Untagged group members join the released line, which reverses my earlier recommendation to change the code for VER-GRP-06.
  - The Cargo commands run from the governing workspace.
  - Four other spec edits.
- **Tests and checks:** each code fix has a unit test, and the contract test has 31 cases. The lib tests for `callisto-graph`, `callisto-manifests` and `callisto-cli` pass, as do clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, shellcheck, and `callisto status --check`. Four changesets are included.

**Release workflow:** the runs for #424, #426 and #425 all finished successfully. Releases are healthy, but the hold workflow's draft-and-restore path still hasn't run, because no release PR has been open since #425.

**Not in #427, listed on the trail:** five release-code bugs. The `--dry-run` failure (E170) with an artifact and no `origin` is the most visible. The trust-check order on shallow and SHA-256 clones, the `--artifact-repository` usage error, the tag probe echoing stderr, and the JSON error envelope's `command` key are the others. There are also seven test-only gaps. I'd do those next as their own PRs.

**Still open from earlier:**
- The private-root exclusion shape needs your decision.
- The OIDC decisions are open.
- Trail closing is still blocked for the 15 merged trails.
- The leftover worktrees and `stack/docs-v1` are still there.

Merge #427 when CI is green. Say which code bug you want first.

content.text:
No. `--help` and `-h` on every command are enough, and Callisto already disables clap's `help` subcommand on purpose (`disable_help_subcommand = true` in `cli.rs:7`). The spec lists it as hidden. The bug was only that completions offered `help` under `pre` and `release`, where `callisto pre help` exits 2 as unrecognized. #427 makes completions match what actually parses.

I'd keep it that way:
- **Why `help` is rarely worth it:** it's a `git` and `cargo` convention. Offering it everywhere means a second spelling of `--help` for every subcommand, in `--help` output and completions, plus more surface to test.
- **The cost of the alternative:** enabling it everywhere is a one-line change, but it makes the spec's "hidden" claim false and adds `help` to every command list.
- **One thing I didn't check:** `callisto help` at the root printed the top-level help in my test, but I didn't look at its exit code. If you want a consistent rule, "`help` nowhere, `--help` everywhere" is the simplest, and I'd add one test that `callisto help` and `callisto pre help` behave the same.

Want me to add that test to #427, or leave it as is?

content.text:
The `help` test is added and pushed to #427. It confirms `callisto help release plan` parses and that `pre help` and `release help` don't. The `callisto-cli` lib tests in `cli::tests` pass, and the commit is signed.

This list comes from what I verified today, not from a fresh audit. Items marked "decision" need you before I can start.

## Bug fixes (next, in order)
1. **`release --dry-run` fails with E170 in a workspace with an artifact and no `origin`.** This is the most visible. The spec says a preview must work without a remote.
2. **Trust-check order.** On a shallow clone or SHA-256 repository, `release plan --from-release-commit` fails with E164 or E224 instead of E266 or E265, because the check runs too late.
3. **`release plan --artifact-repository` without `--orchestration-revision`** gives a clap usage error, not E231 or the ignore notice.
4. **The origin tag probe prints git's stderr** in `release --dry-run` when the origin is unreachable.
5. **JSON error envelope.** On failure it reports `command: release` for `release plan` and omits `dryRun` for the release-pr subcommands.
6. **Add the seven test-only gaps.** These are MX-OUT-02, MX-ERR-06, MX-ERR-07, MX-DISC-02, WS-ID-08, WS-ID-09 and VER-CS-03.
7. **Verify the hold workflow's draft-and-restore path** on the next real release PR.

## Performance
- **No work worth starting.** The A/B showed no regression at 10,000 packages, only a repeatable 20 ms gap at 400 packages (suspects #418 and #415).
- **Optional:** bisect that gap. I'd skip it by your measure-first rule.

## DX and UX
- **Private workspace root listed as a package** (decision). `publish-to = ["none"]` already stops publishing, but the package still shows in `status`.
- **Fixed groups can't share one tag or GitHub release title** (E194). It needs a design pass on ADRs 9 and 12.
- **Use the `uses: $/...` lines in the workflows** only after confirming they are what they appear to be.
- **Pre-merge feedback.** A `status`-style warning on the release PR when it is stale would make the draft hold visible, instead of just blocking the merge.

## Feature work
- **OIDC trusted publishing**, npm first (decision). The owner raised its priority because michi's `NPM_TOKEN` type is being deprecated. It needs the config-shape choice and whether Callisto's own release workflow may hold `id-token: write`.
- **Waiting on michi:** the `ready_by_edge` swap, once michi releases it.
- **T12:** production-path registry tests for Cargo and PyPI, which `registry_endpoint.rs` currently blocks by rejecting non-https and loopback URLs. Decide an approach or drop it.
- **ADR 12 and the other owner decisions** (immutable releases, private PyPI, checksums).

**My pick:** items 1 to 4 in one PR, since they're all in the release command's error paths, then OIDC once you've answered the two questions. Say go on the bug-fix PR, or answer the OIDC questions.

version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: [release-candidate, drain]
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      ((needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
        needs.drain.result == 'skipped' && inputs.release_source_sha == '') ||
       (needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true' &&
        needs.drain.result == 'success' && needs.drain.outputs.has_pending == 'false'))
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # Interdependent Cargo packages bump together, so Cargo.lock must be refreshed in the release PR.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Keeps one comment on the release PR that says why it is held, so a draft needs no trip to the Actions tab.
# Source it and call `release_pr_note`, or run it: release-pr-note.sh <held|ready|failed> <pr-number> [run-url]
# Needs GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY; GITHUB_SHA names the push the note is about.
set -euo pipefail

release_pr_note() {
  local state="$1" pr="$2" run_url="${3:-}"
  local marker='<!-- callisto-release-pr-state -->'
  local short="${GITHUB_SHA:0:7}" body existing
  case "$state" in
    held)
      body="Held as a draft: \`main\` moved to \`$short\`, so this PR may be stale. The Release workflow marks it ready after it rebuilds the PR from the new tip."
      ;;
    ready)
      body="Ready: rebuilt from \`main\` at \`$short\`."
      ;;
    failed)
      body="Still a draft: the Release workflow could not rebuild this PR from \`main\` at \`$short\`. See ${run_url:-the Release workflow runs}, fix the cause and re-run it; the PR becomes ready when the rebuild succeeds."
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown release PR state: $state" >&2
      return 2
      ;;
  esac
  body="$marker"$'\n'"$body"
  existing=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$pr/comments" \
    --jq ".[] | select(.body | startswith(\"$marker\")) | .id" | sed -n 1p)
  if [[ -n "$existing" ]]; then
    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/comments/$existing" -f body="$body" > /dev/null
  else
    gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$pr/comments" -f body="$body" > /dev/null
  fi
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]; then
  release_pr_note "${1:?usage: release-pr-note.sh <held|ready|failed> <pr-number> [run-url]}" "${2:?pr number}" "${3:-}"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drafts the open managed release PR as soon as main moves, because a draft cannot be merged. The release
# workflow marks it ready again only after a refresh built from the new tip, so a failed or skipped refresh
# leaves a stale release PR unmergeable instead of mergeable. Usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>
# Needs GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
set -euo pipefail

release_branch="${1:?usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>}"

prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,headRefName,headRepository)
numbers=$(jq -r --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --arg branch "$release_branch" '
  .[] | select(.isDraft == false
    and (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // "") == $repo
    and (.headRefName == $branch or (.headRefName | startswith($branch + "--")))) | .number' <<< "$prs")

for number in $numbers; do
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if gh pr ready "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --undo; then
      echo "::notice::Held release PR #$number as a draft until the release workflow refreshes it"
      break
    fi
    [[ $attempt -lt 3 ]] || { echo "::error::could not draft release PR #$number"; exit 1; }
    sleep $((attempt * 2))
  done
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Keeps one comment on the release PR that says why it is held, so a draft needs no trip to the Actions tab.
# Source it and call `release_pr_note`, or run it: release-pr-note.sh <held|ready|failed> <pr-number> [run-url]
# Needs GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY; GITHUB_SHA names the push the note is about.
set -euo pipefail

release_pr_note() {
  local state="$1" pr="$2" run_url="${3:-}"
  local marker='<!-- callisto-release-pr-state -->'
  local short="${GITHUB_SHA:0:7}" body existing
  case "$state" in
    held)
      body="Held as a draft: \`main\` moved to \`$short\`, so this PR may be stale. The Release workflow marks it ready after it rebuilds the PR from the new tip."
      ;;
    ready)
      body="Ready: rebuilt from \`main\` at \`$short\`."
      ;;
    failed)
      body="Still a draft: the Release workflow could not rebuild this PR from \`main\` at \`$short\`. See ${run_url:-the Release workflow runs}, fix the cause and re-run it; the PR becomes ready when the rebuild succeeds."
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown release PR state: $state" >&2
      return 2
      ;;
  esac
  body="$marker"$'\n'"$body"
  existing=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$pr/comments" \
    --jq ".[] | select(.body | startswith(\"$marker\")) | .id" | sed -n 1p)
  if [[ -n "$existing" ]]; then
    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/comments/$existing" -f body="$body" > /dev/null
  else
    gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$pr/comments" -f body="$body" > /dev/null
  fi
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]; then
  release_pr_note "${1:?usage: release-pr-note.sh <held|ready|failed> <pr-number> [run-url]}" "${2:?pr number}" "${3:-}"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavior test for the release PR state comment (release-pr-note.sh) and the rebuild note (note-release-pr-rebuild.sh), with a stubbed gh.
set -u
scripts="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../scripts" && pwd)"
fail=0

run_case() { # <script> <pr list json> <existing comment ids> <script args...>
  local script="$1" pr_list="$2" comment_ids="$3"
  shift 3
  local calls harness
  calls="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  harness="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/callisto.XXXXXX")"
  cat > "$harness" <<'STUBS'
gh() {
  echo "gh $*" >> "$CALLS_FILE"
  case "$1" in
    pr) printf '%s\n' "$PR_LIST" ;;
    api)
      if [[ " $* " == *'/comments '* && " $* " != *' -X '* ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$COMMENT_IDS"
      fi ;;
  esac
}
STUBS
  CALLS_FILE="$calls" PR_LIST="$pr_list" COMMENT_IDS="$comment_ids" GITHUB_REPOSITORY='orin-dx/callisto' \
    GITHUB_SHA='0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567' \
    bash -c 'source "$1"; script=$2; shift 2; source "$script" "$@"' -- "$harness" "$scripts/$script" "$@" > /dev/null 2>&1
  local code=$?
  printf '%s\n---calls---\n' "$code"
  grep -v 'api --paginate' "$calls" | cut -c1-400
  rm -f "$calls" "$harness"
}

pr() { # <number> <branch> <draft>
  printf '[{"number":%s,"headRefName":"%s","isDraft":%s,"headRepository":{"nameWithOwner":"orin-dx/callisto"}}]' "$1" "$2" "$3"
}
verdict() { if [[ "$2" == 0 ]]; then echo "PASS: $1"; else echo "FAIL: $1"; fail=1; fi; }
ok=1

# The state comment is created once and then edited in place.
output="$(run_case release-pr-note.sh '[]' '' held 7)"
if [[ "$output" == 0$'\n'* && "$output" == *'-X POST repos/orin-dx/callisto/issues/7/comments'* && "$output" == *'Held as a draft'* && "$output" == *'0123456'* ]]; then ok=0; else ok=1; fi
verdict 'a first note creates the comment' "$ok"

output="$(run_case release-pr-note.sh '[]' '555' ready 7)"
if [[ "$output" == 0$'\n'* && "$output" == *'-X PATCH repos/orin-dx/callisto/issues/comments/555'* && "$output" != *'-X POST'* && "$output" == *'Ready: rebuilt'* ]]; then ok=0; else ok=1; fi
verdict 'a later note edits the same comment' "$ok"

output="$(run_case release-pr-note.sh '[]' '' failed 7 https://example.test/run/9)"
if [[ "$output" == 0$'\n'* && "$output" == *'https://example.test/run/9'* && "$output" == *'Still a draft'* ]]; then ok=0; else ok=1; fi

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Time `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and count their git processes.
# `CALLISTO_BENCH_PACKAGES=50,200` picks the sizes.
bench:
    cargo bench -p callisto-cli --bench commands

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's real shell block with Git and GitHub API
# boundaries faked. This proves the script's control flow given a decision
# shape; it does not call the real `callisto` binary, so it cannot catch a
# mismatch between what Callisto actually serializes and what this script's
# jq expressions expect. See test-release-action-binary for that check.
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# Run Clippy lints (warnings treated as errors) as a single workspace invocation.
# Moon's per-project `cargo clippy -p $project` tasks all lock the same shared
# target/ dir, so running them one-per-project serializes on Cargo's own build
# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's
# internal job scheduler parallelize across crates instead.
lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
audit: license-boundary
    cargo deny check

# callisto-model is MIT: nothing it depends on at build or run time, directly or not, may be FSL-licensed or a Callisto FSL crate.
license-boundary:
    ! cargo tree -p callisto-model -e normal,build --prefix none --format '{p} {l}' | grep -E 'FSL|callisto-(manifests|graph|cli|fixtures)'

# Compile the fuzz targets so they cannot rot (running them needs nightly and cargo-fuzz)
fuzz-check:
    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# The shipped binary is built with the features its crates default to, and none of them is the dev-only `test-util`.
features-boundary:
    ! cargo tree -p callisto-cli -e normal,build -f '{p} {f}' | grep 'test-util'

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Generate code coverage report via cargo-llvm-cov.
#
# Optional `threshold`: when set, fails if total line coverage drops below
# it (--fail-under-lines). The human-readable summary is always emitted
# before enforcing the threshold: LCOV output itself contains no aggregate
# percentage, and a failed CI gate must say what developers need to improve.
# Unset means informational only; `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`,
# so a CI coverage failure always reproduces locally with the same invocation.
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
    fi

# Check per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%). The
# workspace-total --fail-under-lines gate can pass while a small crate is
# far below threshold, since a few large crates dominate the total line
# count -- this catches that case. Requires profile data from a prior
# `cargo llvm-cov` run in this session (e.g. `just coverage` just ran, or
# CI's own coverage step ran first); does not re-run tests itself.
coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json
    report=$(jq -r '
        .data[0].files[]
        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0

pre-commit: fmt-check

pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

release-workflow-checks:
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh

# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.

    bash .github/tests/test-hold-release-pr.sh

    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_contract.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_download_extraction_format.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh

# release-PR decide contract and artifact preflight build. CI runs them as

ci: fmt-check lint fuzz-check test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior (coverage "90")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drafts the open managed release PR as soon as main moves, because a draft cannot be merged. The release
# workflow marks it ready again only after a refresh built from the new tip, so a failed or skipped refresh
# leaves a stale release PR unmergeable instead of mergeable. Usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>
# Needs GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
set -euo pipefail

release_branch="${1:?usage: hold-release-pr.sh <release-branch>}"

# shellcheck source=release-pr-note.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/release-pr-note.sh"

prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,headRefName,headRepository)
numbers=$(jq -r --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --arg branch "$release_branch" '
  .[] | select(.isDraft == false
    and (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // "") == $repo
    and (.headRefName == $branch or (.headRefName | startswith($branch + "--")))) | .number' <<< "$prs")

for number in $numbers; do
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if gh pr ready "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --undo; then
      echo "::notice::Held release PR #$number as a draft until the release workflow refreshes it"
      release_pr_note held "$number" || echo "::warning::could not write the hold note on release PR #$number"
      break
    fi
    [[ $attempt -lt 3 ]] || { echo "::error::could not draft release PR #$number"; exit 1; }
    sleep $((attempt * 2))
  done
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Writes how the release PR rebuild ended on the PR's state comment (see hold-release-pr.sh for how it got held).
# Usage: note-release-pr-rebuild.sh <release-branch> <success|failure> <run-url>
# Needs GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_REPOSITORY and GITHUB_SHA. A rebuild that ended with the PR still a draft, because main moved
# again, leaves the hold note: a newer run is already on its way.
set -euo pipefail

release_branch="${1:?usage: note-release-pr-rebuild.sh <release-branch> <success|failure> <run-url>}"
outcome="${2:?outcome}"
run_url="${3:?run url}"

# shellcheck source=release-pr-note.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/release-pr-note.sh"

prs=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,headRefName,headRepository)
found=$(jq -r --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --arg branch "$release_branch" '
  [.[] | select((.headRepository.nameWithOwner // "") == $repo
    and (.headRefName == $branch or (.headRefName | startswith($branch + "--"))))][0]
  | if . == null then "" else "\(.number) \(.isDraft)" end' <<< "$prs")
[[ -n "$found" ]] || exit 0
read -r number is_draft <<< "$found"

case "$outcome" in
  success)
    if [[ "$is_draft" == false ]]; then release_pr_note ready "$number"; fi
    ;;
  failure)
    release_pr_note failed "$number" "$run_url"
    ;;
esac

So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. One comment on the PR says which: that it is held, that it is ready, or, after a failed rebuild, a link to the failed run. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is retried up to four times before it fails.

If a stale release PR was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the merge consumed no changesets, and every later push to `main` retries it. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.

Status: Accepted (implemented in #154)

## Decision

An existing tag is the planned tag when it names the planned commit and is annotated. Annotation text is not compared, locally or remotely. A lightweight tag or a tag on another commit is a conflict (E167) and is never adopted.

## Options considered

- **Compare the annotation text on both sides** — rejected: the remote side needs the tag object fetched first, and a tag created by a person or an earlier template would block every rerun.

17	- Keep ADR 11's default tag, `{display id}@{version}`, and never rename existing tags. A package takes only the tags its commit shows it made, and `previous-tag-templates` declares a rename.
18	- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.

20	- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
21	- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.

27	
28	- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
29	- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
30	- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.
31	
32	## Consequences
33	
34	Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. # 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision, including its default tag; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. The evidence is in `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.

## Proposed decision

- Require canonical slash-qualified distribution references (`cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name`, `pypi/name`) in `callisto.toml` (groups, package rules, product and artifact packages), in report and matrix keys, and in command-line arguments. Reject the colon form everywhere. A `pypi/` reference uses the declared name. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names and resolve them when read. A changeset entry names the owner package, not a distribution, and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli` (ADR 1).
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Release ownership is derived, not stored: the owner of a package's shared tag, forge release and announcement is its first release id by ecosystem priority Cargo, npm, PyPI. The intent digest seals it and `release execute` re-derives it, so no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.
- Keep ADR 11's default tag, `{display id}@{version}`, and never rename existing tags. A package takes only the tags its commit shows it made, and `previous-tag-templates` declares a rename.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner: selecting one distribution of a package releases all of them, a product's announcement waits for the tag of each package whose asset it carries, and a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.
- Co-located Cargo and Maturin, whose Python version is derived from Cargo, is after v1.

Channel and private-registry policies are not decided here and are not release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- System findings and verification limits: `git show 07154021c:docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md`.

content.text:
Five PRs are open (#427 to #431), and four of the five trails are done. The fifth, #179, is deliberately not built because it needs your decisions. CI is still running on all of them except #427, where all 17 checks are green. The other four have between 1 and 16 checks still pending, and none has a reported failure. `Entire Gates` on each needs your approval of its trail.

## Trails and PRs
| Trail | PR | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| #173 | #427 | Spec-drift fixes, plus the draft-first release PR. CI is green. |
| #176 | #428 | Four release-command bugs fixed (see below). |
| #177 | #429 | A failing command's JSON error carries its report's `command` and `dryRun`. |
| #178 | #430 | Tests for the seven spec criteria that had none. Test-only. |
| #180 | #431 | A comment on the held release PR says why it is held. |
| #179 | none | Verified facts and a recommendation only. |

**#428 fixes:**
- `release --dry-run` works without `origin` when the release builds artifacts.
- `release plan` checks the repository first, so a shallow clone gives E266 and a SHA-256 repository gives E265.
- `--artifact-repository` alone gives E231, not a usage error.
- The origin tag probe is quiet.

**Verification:**
- **Passing:** each fix has a test. Formatting, clippy, shellcheck, the workflow checks and the relevant lib and integration suites pass locally. The polyglot lifecycle test needs network, so it passes outside the sandbox.
- **Not verified:** the comment on a real held release PR. The first push to `main` with an open release PR is the first real run, and CI hasn't finished on the new PRs.

## Needs your decision: trail #179
- **Private root listed as a package.** I confirmed it: a private root with a version shows as `npm/monorepo 0.0.0`, and `publish-to = ["none"]` doesn't hide it. I recommend an explicit `ignore = true` on `[[package]]`. Yes or no?
- **E194 (fixed groups sharing one tag).** It depends on accepting ADR 12, which is still Proposed. Accept it, or tell me what to revise.

## Order to merge
Merge #427 first, then #431, which touches the same release criterion and needs a rebase. The rest are independent.

## Found along the way
Git's own error text can leak onto stderr before the JSON error, for example "not a git repository" or "bad object". I worked around it in the tests but didn't fix it. It deserves its own trail if you want it.

content.content:
entire review — Run a multi-agent review against a branch
Run a multi-agent review against the current branch or a --target branch:
several reviewer agents review the change in parallel, then a single judge consolidates their
reports into the final verdict in a closing round. Reviews are saved as named
profiles in Entire settings and clone-local preferences. On first run, guided
setup writes a profile and asks before starting agents.

Flags:
  --configure    set up a review profile (shows available agents + profiles).
                 With --set-* flags it writes the profile non-interactively;
                 otherwise it opens the wizard (interactive) without starting agents.
  --set-agents   with --configure: comma-separated reviewer agents for the profile
  --set-judge    with --configure: the consolidating judge as agent[=model]
  --set-output   with --configure: where the verdict goes: local (default) or trail
  --local        with --configure: save to .entire/settings.local.json (just you)
                 instead of .entire/settings.json (shared). Interactive setup asks.
  --set-task     with --configure: the profile's canonical task text
  --set-model    with --configure: per-reviewer model as agent=model (repeatable)
  --set-slot     with --configure: a reviewer slot as agent[=model] (repeatable;
                 the same agent/model may repeat to run it multiple times)
  --set-config   with --configure: a reviewer's own agent config as
                 reviewer=<config.json|isolated|none> (repeatable). It replaces
                 the reviewed checkout's hooks, MCP servers and extensions; the
                 checkout's skills still load. Saved to clone-local preferences.
  --edit         re-open the advanced profile skill picker
  --findings     browse local findings; pass a handle to print one saved run
  --agent NAME   run only one reviewer from the selected profile
  --list         list configured review profiles (their reviewers and judge)
  --agents       list the reviewer agents you can pass to --agent for the profile
  --model NAME   override the model for the --agent reviewer (requires --agent)

I couldn't find any saved code-review or "slop" agent findings, so I built the pattern list from what we found today and swept the codebase for each pattern.

**Where I looked:**
- Entire has no findings on any of the 36 callisto changes, no review profiles, and no saved local review runs.
- The repo has no "slop" agent. The only "slop" mention in past transcripts is a line in the memory index ("no AI slop").
- The last review document is `V1-REVIEW-2026-10-20` in the local plans, which led to the spec re-check we already finished.
- If those findings live elsewhere (a plugin I don't have, or a specific past session), point me at them and I'll mine those too.

**Patterns from today, and where else they appear:**
1. **A command substitution doesn't inherit `set -e`, so a failed read is hidden.** The only remaining sites are the five `"$(release_pr_snapshot)"` arguments in `create-or-update-release-pr.sh`, and #427 fixes those. Nothing else in `.github/` has the pattern.
2. **A hardcoded `.changeset/pre.json` path in an error message.** E115 is fixed in #427. Still hardcoded:
   - E114 (`graph/error.rs:294-297`);
   - two CLI help texts (`cli/error.rs:110` and `:317`).
   The `[changesets] dir` setting can move the file, so these say the wrong path.
3. **A probe whose failure is expected uses the live-echo runner, so the tool's own error reaches the terminal.** I saw this today as "not a git repository" and "bad object" ahead of the JSON error. Candidates:
   - `init.rs:197,202`
   - `tag.rs:109, 254, 281`
   - `release_decision.rs:733`
   - `artifact.rs:86` and `forge.rs:215`, which are `gh` calls
   Each needs a look to see whether its failure is expected. #428 already fixed the origin tag probe.
4. **clap constraints that pre-empt a typed error.** `cli.rs:366-376` (`conflicts_with` and `required_unless_present` between `--package` and `--from-release-commit`) and `:456` (`requires = "artifact_manifest"`) aren't checked yet. #428 removes the one at `:360`.
5. **A byte-order mark handled in one parser but not another.** I fixed `npm_declares_private` and `npm_role_from_source` in #427. Not yet checked: `membership.rs:602` and `npm.rs:318`. `root.rs` is fine.

I haven't verified any of these candidates beyond the greps. A deeper pass is a good job for the `bug-hunter` agent, with each pattern as a brief.

Next, I'd file one trail ("Expected failures stay quiet and name the real path") and fix patterns 2 to 5 in one PR, verifying each site first. Say go, or send me the findings source.

content.text:
Yes, there's much more to find, and today's run shows the limit of how I did it. Each reviewer read only part of its crate, and each said so in its report. A thorough pass needs a coverage-driven loop, not one fan-out. Below is a reusable plan and a prompt you can paste into any repo.

## The plan

| Phase | Who | Model / effort | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Measure | Scripts only, no LLM | none | A hotspot table: lines per file, comment ratio, history-word comments, `allow` attributes, string literals repeated more than twice, bare `is_ok`/`is_err` asserts, unused exports |
| 1. Shard review | One read-only agent per shard of 5k to 8k lines, ranked by hotspot score | Sonnet 5.5, medium | Structured findings plus a coverage manifest (files read and not read) |
| 2. Cross-cutting | One agent per pattern across the whole repo: duplicated logic, literal tables, error paths, test quality | Sonnet 5.5, medium | Findings with both sites named |
| 3. Risk hunt | One agent per risky module (release, publish, auth, path handling) | Opus 5.5, high | Adversarial bug findings, not style |
| 4. Verify | One agent per top-N finding, given the code and not the claim | Haiku 5.5 for quote and existence checks, Sonnet 5.5 for behavior | Confirmed or refuted, with evidence |
| 5. Spec drift | One agent per spec file, reproducing behavior on the built binary | Sonnet 5.5, medium | Covered, drifted or uncovered per criterion |
| 6. Synthesize | Main thread | Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.1, high | Ranked backlog, trails, and a guard per pattern |
| 7. Fix | Sequential, one PR per pattern per crate | Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 | PRs |

The rules behind it:
- **Coverage loop:** any shard whose manifest shows unread hotspots gets another agent, until nothing important is unread. This is what "very thorough" costs, and today's runs skipped it.
- **Verify cheaply:** a refuter that sees code and not your conclusion is far less likely to just confirm it.
- **Fan out only to read:** parallel agents investigate. Fixes go one at a time, with a targeted test after each, because coupled changes break when parallelized.
- **Guards:** every pattern ends as a CI check, so it cannot come back.
- **Rough cost:** today's four sampled reviewers used about 410k tokens for roughly a third of the code. A full pass over this repo would be on the order of 1M to 1.5M tokens for phases 1 to 4. That estimate comes from today's usage, not a measurement.

## Master prompt (paste into the main session)

```
Goal: find every place this repo has the problems below, rank them, and propose a guard for each pattern. Read-only until I approve fixes.

Rules for you and every agent:
- No builds or tests in a shared checkout; read-only tools, plus the already-built binary on throwaway fixtures where a behavior claim needs proof.
- Every finding needs file:line, a quoted line, a category, a confidence, and a one-line fix. Unverified inference is not a finding.
- Report counts, not essays. Each agent reports under 900 words as structured JSON.
- Each agent must return a coverage manifest: files fully read, files sampled, files not read. Unread hotspots are queued for another agent.
- Project style rules (read them from the repo's docs first): comments are one short line, only for a non-obvious reason; tests must name the error they expect; one definition per string.

Categories: (1) comments that restate code, narrate history, or run long; (2) dead code and unused exports; (3) needless wrappers; (4) duplicated logic and copied test helpers; (5) defensive code for ruled-out states; (6) tests that assert nothing real; (7) hardcoded or repeated values (tool names, env names, paths, versions, branch names); (8) names or docs that disagree with code; (9) expected-failure probes that leak a tool's own stderr; (10) checks done after use instead of before; (11) framework constraints that pre-empt a typed error; (12) one parser handling an input quirk (BOM, CRLF, case) that its siblings do not; (13) spec or docs that disagree with the code.

Steps:
0. Run mechanical sweeps (script, no LLM) and print the hotspot table.
1. Shard the source by hotspot score; launch one read-only Sonnet agent per shard with the rules above.
2. Launch one agent per cross-cutting pattern on the whole repo.
3. Launch Opus agents for the riskiest modules only, with an adversarial bug brief.
4. For the top 40 findings, launch a verifier that is given the code location and the category but not my conclusion.
5. Loop on coverage manifests until no hotspot is unread.
6. Merge into one ranked list: reader cost removed times risk. Group into trails by outcome, not by file.
7. For each pattern, propose a CI check (grep or lint) that would have caught it.
```

## Shard agent prompt (template)

```
Read-only slop and bug review of <paths>. Do not edit or build. Apply categories 1 to 13 above. For each category give a count and the five highest-value instances as `file:line | quoted line | why | fix`. Verify each by reading the surrounding code. End with the files you did not read and the three patterns in this shard worth a rule. Under 900 words.
```

Next, I can write this as a Workflow script (I'd load the workflow-authoring reference first) or save it as a skill you can reuse in other repos. Which do you want?

This is from the caliper look at its findings too:



<pasted_content id="6d4c">
These patterns come from 71 findings in this repo, so they're hypotheses for other repos, not verified there. Roughly in order of how likely they are to bite elsewhere:

1. Hand-copied lists that drift.
   - What we saw: Option names written out in six places, a duplicated schema-version file, and a TypeScript union missing a variant Rust emits.
   - Check elsewhere: Wherever one concept (an option, an enum, a version) is spelled out in more than one file or language, add a single list plus a test or satisfies that fails when they differ.
2. String keys across a boundary.
   - What we saw: less precise read as less_precise, so a metric was always zero.
   - Check elsewhere: Look for stringly-typed keys passed between languages or processes. A missing key should fail loudly, not default to zero.
3. Graceful degradation applied to the wrong errors.
   - What we saw: Swallowed panics, an addon that logs provider errors at debug level and falls through to another engine, ignored exit codes, and dropped inputs with no count.
   - Check elsewhere: Soft failure suits user input. Misconfiguration, missing binaries and internal panics need a loud failure. Grep for catch {}, .ok(), unwrap_or_default(), || true and continue on unmatched entries.
4. Harnesses that don't match the real consumer.
   - What we saw: Benchmarks and measurements ran with the CLI's collapse default, but the Storybook addon uses a different one. Timings also mixed warm caches against cold, and fewer than N samples were reported as N.
   - Check elsewhere: Diff every benchmark invocation against how the real consumer calls the tool. Write the config into the report, and keep instrumentation out of the timed region.
5. Docs written from intent, not from code.
   - What we saw: "Glob patterns" that were substring matches, "five entry points" when there were 15, and numbers nobody could reproduce.
   - Check elsewhere: Recompute the numeric claims in prose, grep every doc word like "always" or "never" against the code, and cite generated records instead of copying numbers. A CI check that referenced paths and commands exist catches stale instructions.
6. Tests that never run or only prove the author's fixture.
   - What we saw: 71 Python tests in no CI job, and tests built from hand-written fixtures that never parse real output.
   - Check elsewhere: For every test file, find what invokes it. Add one end-to-end test per option and one golden test over real output.
7. Heuristics presented as facts.
   - What we saw: A label set purely by text length stated as a count in the docs, and a reference scored against one method that was reported as strong evidence.
   - Check elsewhere: Say what a metric measures. If a category is a threshold guess, name it that.
8. Unverified agent output turned into conclusions.
   - What we saw: I repeated worker numbers as fact, and two of my claims were wrong.
   - Check elsewhere: Have a different agent re-check any number before it is stated, and have authors self-review for unused parameters, stale comments and silent drops. Run the automated review on measurement and script code, not only product code.
9. Dead code and history comments.
   - What we saw: Unused fields behind #[allow(dead_code)] and about 14 "previously / now" comments.
   - Check elsewhere: Count and justify every allow attribute, and delete comments that narrate history.

Patterns 1, 3, 4 and 6 had the highest cost in our review, because each changed a conclusion or hid a bug in shipped code.

The cheap mechanical checks that travel to other repos are the greps in items 3 and 5, an audit of which test files CI runs, and a list of where each option name appears.

I could turn this into a short checklist file and a reusable review prompt, so other repos or workers can run the same sweep. Is that useful?
</pasted_content id="6d4c">
